name: Kinetic offer wall

operations.name: Suggest options from a website
operations.agentTask: Read the website in `sourceUrl` and write three different ways to fill the ad "Kinetic offer wall". Objective: Make one legitimate offer readable while showing the product range. Visual rule: The offer is the hero; repetition creates texture but never competes with the readable offer. Beats, in order: - 0–1.5 s: Oversized offer occupies the upper-middle canvas; one pack is already visible. Shows Brand color, Hero product, Offer. - 1.5–4 s: Three products share a consistent center and baseline. Shows Brand color, Hero product, Product 2, Product 3, Range name. - 4–6.5 s: Hero product grows while repeated copy recedes. Shows Brand color, Hero product, Benefit. - 6.5–8.5 s: Offer, eligible product range and end date become a stable card. Shows Brand color, Hero product, Product 2, Product 3, Offer terms. - 8.5–10 s: Stable brand/product/CTA lockup. Shows Brand color, Hero product, Logo, Call to action. Use only facts the website or pages you read state. Never invent prices, discounts, dates, guarantees or claims. When a fact a field needs is missing, write a short placeholder in square brackets, such as [offer end date]. Make the three options clearly different in angle, wording and image choice. For images, choose real, large images of this brand and product: first from the page's own images (header logo, large files, feature-page screenshots), then with an image search. A social preview card (og:image, a title on a gradient) is a last resort. Give the direct URL of the image file, never a page URL, and never an image of another brand. Use an empty string when no image fits. If image search throws because no search backend is configured, tell the user in one sentence that a SerpAPI, DataForSEO or Brave key in Settings finds better images. Then take nodetool.web.screenshot of the product's feature pages instead. Save each image you consider as an asset and look at it with view_image before you offer it. Name in the option's description any image that is only a social preview card. Write `fillOptions` as a list of three objects, `fillChoice` as "" and `fillReport` as "". Each option: - value: "1", "2" or "3" - title: a name for the direction in 2 to 4 words - description: one sentence on what it emphasizes, then the first two copy lines in quotes - image: the URL of its first image, for the option card - brandColor: the brand's accent color as #RRGGBB (buttons, links, highlights), not the page background or a theme-color that is near black or white - fields: offerShort (Offer: hook, at most 7 words); collectionLabel (Range name: range, at most 7 words); benefitShort (Benefit: benefit, at most 7 words); offerTerms (Offer terms: proof of offer, at most 16 words); cta (Call to action: cta, at most 4 words) - images: product1 (Hero product: A shot of the product alone, ideally on a plain or transparent background, so it reads as a cutout. Shown in: Oversized offer occupies the upper-middle canvas; one pack is already visible. | Three products share a consistent center and baseline. | Hero product grows while repeated copy recedes. | Offer, eligible product range and end date become a stable card. | Stable brand/product/CTA lockup.); product2 (Product 2: A shot of the product alone, ideally on a plain or transparent background, so it reads as a cutout. Shown in: Three products share a consistent center and baseline. | Offer, eligible product range and end date become a stable card.); product3 (Product 3: A shot of the product alone, ideally on a plain or transparent background, so it reads as a cutout. Shown in: Three products share a consistent center and baseline. | Offer, eligible product range and end date become a stable card.); logo (Logo: The brand's own logo file, such as the site header logo or its icon. Shown in: Stable brand/product/CTA lockup.) Then show the Start step with `only: ["fillChoice"]` and a one-sentence note, so the user sees just the option cards. Picking one runs `apply`, which saves the images and fills the steps.
